rationale: All five proofs are mathematically correct, with the compressed running-minimum arguments requiring only routine inferences. A is the most economical and direct: successive minimizations establish the slope inequalities, and one explicit inequality chain forces B to lie sufficiently close to A. C offers the same elementary mechanism with excellent signposting and explicitly identifies continuity as the sufficient regularity, but adds slightly more scaffolding. B clearly announces its strategy and supplies detailed justification of Lipschitz continuity and the existence of nearby contacts, although its differentiation argument is more elaborate than the minimization approach. D compresses those justifications while retaining a useful opening overview; E is similarly sound but gives less strategic guidance and uses “contact points” without explicitly defining the term.
